name: USDD
oneLiner: USDD is the Tron DAO Reserve's CDP-and-PSM stablecoin, designed as overcollateralized but historically traded below peg through multiple stress episodes.
collateral: Current reserves are split across Smart Allocator stablecoin deployments, TRX and sTRX CDP vault collateral, and USDT held in PSM/direct vaults; Bitcoin was removed from reserves in August 2024
pegMechanism: CDP model with minimum 130% collateral ratio; Peg Stability Module enables 1:1 minting/redemption against USDT and USDC

oracleRisk.summary: USDD CDP collateral prices pass through per-collateral Median, OSM, and Spot modules before reaching Vat, with Chainlink and WinkLink documented as the primary feed sources.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 data research
branchApplicability.rationale: USDD supports governed CDP collateral types with per-ilk oracle modules, collateral ratios, liquidation parameters, and auction contracts. The documented collateral types share one Median-to-OSM-to-Spot and Dog-to-Clipper mechanism family; PSM stablecoin conversion is a fixed-price issuance rail rather than a collateral-liquidation branch.

branches.label: USDD governed CDP collateral types
branches.summary: Governed USDD collateral types share per-ilk Median, OSM, and Spot pricing followed by Dog and collateral-specific Clipper liquidation auctions.

feeds.path: Supported feeds -> per-collateral Median -> OSM current/next price -> Spot -> Vat

branches.fallbackBehavior: The OSM retains a current value and separately stages the next Median value; if updates stop, Vat continues using the last Spot value and the collateral price can become stale.

collateralParameters.note: Each collateral type has a governed Spot liquidation ratio and Dog liquidation capacity; USDD documentation states the minimum ratio varies by asset and illustrates a 130% liquidation threshold.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When a Vault falls below its collateral-specific minimum ratio, Dog initiates liquidation and the corresponding Clipper sells collateral through a descending-price Dutch auction; proceeds repay USDD debt and penalties and surplus collateral returns to the user.
branches.backstop: Collateral-auction proceeds cover Vault debt; the documented system architecture provides Vow accounting and a Flop debt-auction path that sells governance tokens to recapitalize a protocol deficit.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Uncovered system deficits can proceed to the documented debt-auction path. Deployment records also identify End and ESM contracts on supported CDP chains for emergency shutdown and settlement.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Material USDD supply on Tron, Ethereum, and BSC uses chain-local native token and Join rails. Legacy BTTC predicate representations remain peripheral bridge risk and are not treated as canonical issuance.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 data research

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDD is presented as the TRON DAO Reserve's dollar-pegged stablecoin for payments, with over-collateralized reserves and PSM swap/redemption mechanics.

genius.notes: USDD has self-reported reserve and PSM/redemption disclosures (usdd.io/data), but no formal third-party attestation. No GENIUS PPSI approval, application, or comparability determination for a foreign issuer exception was found. TRON DAO Reserve is Dominica-domiciled; Treasury has not yet finalized criteria for "comparable foreign regulation" under GENIUS. The April 2026 OFAC-coordinated Tether USDT freeze on TRON wallets and May 2026 UK sanctions on HTX are not GENIUS Act enforcement actions against USDD or its issuer.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No GENIUS PPSI approval, official application, state-qualified approval, or registered/comparability-determined foreign-issuer exception was found for USDD or its issuer TRON DAO Reserve. No Treasury determination of comparable foreign regulation has been made for any jurisdiction as of this review date. The GENIUS Act approval framework itself remains in proposed-rulemaking phase.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: USDD's official core-features documentation states that no centralized authority can freeze user funds. The official deployment list covers the reviewed Tron, Ethereum, and BNB Chain token contracts; the verified Ethereum token exposes Maker-style mint, burn, deny, rely, and transfer operations but no holder blacklist or freeze function. USDT/USDC PSM and DeFi reserves can carry upstream freeze exposure, which is separate from a direct USDD holder-balance control.

mintAuthority.summary: USDD uses direct Maker-style token and Join contracts on Tron, Ethereum, and BSC. Each Join can mint only against existing Vat credit/debt accounting; chain-local GovActionsProxy owner paths can immediately change system authorization and limits with no timelock.

controls.label: USDD Tron Join (active ward / direct minter)
controls.evidence: At Tron block 83506136, wards(TronJoin) on the direct USDD token returned 1 and the Tron Vat was live. The Join can mint only while consuming existing Vat credit/debt accounting; it cannot raise the system debt ceiling or authorize itself.

controls.label: USDD Tron GovActionsProxy (governance executor)
controls.evidence: Tron Pause (TNq6E9XsQfrzqVwam67LApZQx1omsj8dyW) authority() = GovActionsProxy (TXzhj9Xh8xfzerjinRyM5TfoBL7Cw5hk5d); Pause delay() = 0 (no timelock). GovActionsProxy.authority() = zero address (no higher authority set); GovActionsProxy govActions() = TDLgCe2SatVew6PxSwYmqsc3zfahqXwuqX and pause() = Pause contract. This contract's cast() function is the system's governance executor. The signer set that can call cast() was not confirmed — authority()=zero means access control falls back to contract-level access checks or is operated by the deployer.

controls.label: USDD Tron GovActionsProxy owner — single-key account (governance executor)
controls.evidence: GovActionsProxy.owner() returned 41b28033...eb069 (TSF2rqLdrrZG7PZkDxtvu6B2PTpofidMAX) via triggerconstantcontract; trongrid getaccount shows a normal account with 1-of-1 owner and active permissions (single keypair, no Tron-native multisig). All recent GovActionsProxy transactions originate from this account; with authority()=zero, ds-auth restricts cast() to this owner.

controls.label: USDD Ethereum Join
controls.evidence: The direct verified Join is authorized to mint the chain-local USDD token only while consuming existing Vat credit/debt accounting. It cannot independently raise the system debt ceiling or authorize itself.

controls.label: USDD Ethereum GovActionsProxy
controls.evidence: This chain-local governance executor can change Vat/Join authorization and debt limits. Its owner path is immediate and the reviewed Pause delay is zero.

controls.label: USDD Ethereum GovActionsProxy owner EOA
controls.evidence: GovActionsProxy.owner() returned this address and eth_getCode returned empty. The EOA can immediately execute governance changes that authorize mint rails or raise system limits.

controls.label: USDD BSC Join
controls.evidence: The direct verified Join is authorized to mint the chain-local USDD token only while consuming existing Vat credit/debt accounting. It cannot independently raise the system debt ceiling or authorize itself.

controls.label: USDD BSC GovActionsProxy
controls.evidence: This chain-local governance executor can change Vat/Join authorization and debt limits. Its owner path is immediate and the reviewed Pause delay is zero.

controls.label: USDD BSC GovActionsProxy owner EOA
controls.evidence: GovActionsProxy.owner() returned this address and eth_getCode returned empty. The EOA can immediately execute governance changes that authorize mint rails or raise system limits.

review.evidence: Deployment-wide review covered the current Tron, Ethereum, and BSC direct token/Join rails. Each Join mints only against Vat credit/debt accounting and cannot independently raise its limit; each chain-local GovActionsProxy owner can immediately change authorization and system limits with no timelock. Ethereum/BSC use the same owner EOA, while Tron uses a 1/1 native account. The tracked token and Join contracts are direct non-proxy deployments with no implementation-replacement surface; legacy BTTC predicate upgrades remain a separate peripheral bridge risk.

reserveReview.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 dependency review
reserveReview.rationale: USDD reports Smart Allocator positions as a protocol aggregate while separately identifying TRX, sTRX, and a fractional USDT PSM reserve holding. The Smart Allocator is classified as one protocol-position exposure because the issuer identifies managed investment platforms but does not publish constituent weights; the USDT relationship is proportional collateral exposure, not a serial mechanism dependency.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: USDD Data Platform latest-collateral API, Tron feed
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Stablecoin positions inside Smart Allocator cannot be assigned individual dependency weights.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The allocator bucket aggregates multiple positions and does not expose stablecoin-level percentages.

notices.title: Historical reserve-governance and depeg risk
notices.message: USDD has a history of peg stress, including a March 2023 depeg around $0.93. In August 2024, Tron DAO Reserve removed roughly 12,000 BTC from USDD collateral without prior DAO approval, leaving reserve governance dependent on Tron DAO Reserve decisions.
